answer: A new agent enters the garden as a low-trust vertex: every action it takes must be backed by a refundable stake that only unlocks after verified useful work. Peers cannot wander between identities to escape a bad record, because reputation is bound to the staked vertex, not the display name. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes and completing a thousand rounds of real work first, so a sybil attack costs more in locked capital and time than any single fake identity can ever earn back.
